Unauthorized.description: The request carries no token, or another one.

Account.description:
One signed-in account at one provider.

An account's identity is `provider` + `org` + `account_id`, so the same person in two organizations is two accounts and their usage never blends.

account_id.description: The provider's id for this account.

display_name.description: What to call the account, usually its email address.

org.description: The organization or workspace the account belongs to, when known.

plan.description: The subscription plan, as the provider names it, when known.

sign_in.description: Where QuotaDial read this account's sign-in, written for people, with `~` for the home folder, such as `the macOS Keychain item "Claude Code-credentials-a1b2c3d4" (CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR ~/.claude-work)`. Never a token. Left out when unknown.

Alerts.description: The alert rules and what they told lately, as `GET /v1/alerts` and the MCP tool `list_alerts` give them.

firings.description: What the rules told in the last week, at most the newest `RECENT_FIRINGS`, oldest first.

requests.description: How many requests the logs hold for the period.

until.description: The end of the period: when the logs were last read.

currency.description: The ISO 4217 currency code of `used` and `limit`.

enabled.description: Whether extra usage is turned on for the account.

used.description: The amount spent this month, in `currency`.

used_pct.description: How much of the monthly extra-usage limit is used, as a percentage.

tightest.description: The window closest to its limit, which sets the headroom: its reset, length and age. For an account that cannot be used now, the last one known.

info.description: The QuotaDial daemon answers on `127.0.0.1` only, at the port in `daemon.json` in QuotaDial's data folder, 47115 unless something else had it. Every request needs the token from the `token` file in the same folder, as `Authorization: Bearer <token>`; without it, or with another, the answer is 401. A request whose `Host` is not `127.0.0.1:<port>` or `localhost:<port>` gets 403, so a web page cannot reach the API through a name of its own. Any other path gets 404 and any other method 405, each with an `Error`. Status and history answer on every copy; headroom and the alert rules are part of QuotaDial Pro, and on QuotaDial Free they answer 403 naming the feature in `pro_feature`.
